items.title: Sub-Part 16: Only the Buddha Is Genuinely Free of Idle Speculation

items.zh: 虛空無鳥迹，外道無沙門。愚夫樂戲論，如來則無有。
items.en: As a bird finds no footing in space, so is there no true renunciant among non-Buddhist paths. Fools delight in idle speculation — but in the Tathāgata there is none.

items.zh: 此頌所明，謂有眾生悕樂勝欲，欲求所攝；又有眾生悕樂勝身，有求所攝；又有眾生悕樂沙門及婆羅門所有解脫，梵行求攝。此中欲求、有求攝者，謂我因少分布施、少分持戒，當得往生善趣天上樂世界中，以妙五欲而自賞納，歡娛遊戲。彼既修習如是願已，得最勝欲及最勝身。譬如眾鳥翱翔虛空，遍虛空中無安足處，如是眾生，於其所得無常諸欲及身分中都無安住，當知亦爾。若樂沙門及婆羅門所有解脫梵行求攝，復有二種。或依善說法，或依惡說法。依惡說法諸外道輩，並無沙門。依善說法邪梵行求所攝受者，亦無沙門。正梵行求所攝受者，得有沙門。又此一切三門所攝，或欲求門、或有求門、或梵行求門。如是皆名樂著戲論。當知如來棄捨一切所有悕求，故無戲論。即以此義，類知如來諸弟子眾，正梵行求所攝受者，亦無戲論。復次，今當略辨上所說義。謂薄伽梵此中略示，離善說法及毘奈耶勤精進者，皆空無益。當知是名此中略義。

items.title: Sub-Part 17: The Genuine Sage, Whom Even the Gods Cannot Recognise

items.zh: 住戲論皆無，踰牆、塹離愛。牟尼遊世間，天人不能識。
items.en: Free of every abode, free of all idle speculation, having crossed the wall and the moat, free of craving — the sage wanders the world, unrecognized by gods or men.

items.zh: 此頌所明，謂阿羅漢苾芻永離貪愛，由四種相，於惡魔怨一切愚夫所繫屬主，解脫自在，隨意遊行空閑聚落。有諸愚夫，遇見如是真阿羅漢，於最究竟自在遊行，不如實知，便於二處妄生輕毀。云何此善男子棄捨自屬養命珍財，乃求屬他資生眾具？何故棄捨生天方便，苦勤精進求有斷滅？是諸愚夫見生天上有勝功德，見處居家有多財產，故於牟尼妄生輕忽。彼所事天，於此牟尼廣大功德尚不能了，況能事者而能識知。云何離愛諸阿羅漢由四種相，於惡魔怨一切愚夫所繫屬主，解脫自在？謂諸愚夫由四識住，為魔怨主之所驅役，令生死中往還五趣；非阿羅漢。又諸愚夫如由重過，為魔怨主之所驅役。謂或增益、或復損減諸惡見故，發起種種執刀杖等惡不善法，墮諸戲論，生諸惡趣，令造種種諸惡業緣；非阿羅漢。又諸愚夫如由中過，為魔怨主之所驅役，令處欲愛繫縛垣牆，不能出離欲界生苦；非阿羅漢。又諸愚夫如由輕過，為魔怨主之所驅役，令生色界及無色界，無明深塹周匝圍繞，閉在生死眾苦牢獄，於生等苦不得出離；非阿羅漢。復次，今當略辨上所說義。謂薄伽梵此中略示，一切愚夫羞不應羞，應羞不羞；於不應怖而生怖見，於應怖中生無怖見。當知是名此中略義。

blocks.text: Two verses about the true renunciant and the true sage. The explanations are **untranslated**.
"As a bird finds no footing in space, so there is no true renunciant among non-Buddhist paths. Fools delight in idle speculation, but in the Tathāgata there is none."

The prose: some beings seek the finest pleasures (seeking desire), some the finest body (seeking existence), some liberation (seeking a holy life). Those who give a little and keep a few precepts in order to enjoy heavenly pleasures do get them, but like birds in the sky, they find no resting place in impermanent pleasure and bodies. Among seekers of liberation, those under wrong teachings have no true renunciant, nor do those in the Buddha's teaching who pursue the holy life wrongly; only those who pursue it rightly do. Master Cháng Bǎi: "renunciant" (śramaṇa) here means the noble path. All three kinds of seeking are "idle speculation" (戲論); the Tathāgata has given up all seeking, and so has none.

subs.head: Crossing the wall and the moat

blocks.text: "Free of every abode, free of all speculation, having crossed the wall and the moat, free of craving: the sage wanders the world, unrecognised by gods or men."

The prose: the arhat, free of craving, is free of Māra, the master of fools, in four ways, and wanders freely. Fools who meet such a one despise him: "Why give up his own wealth to live on others? Why give up the way to heaven to seek annihilation?" Their gods cannot recognise the sage's qualities, still less their worshippers.

The four ways: fools are driven by Māra through the four abodes of consciousness, through the five destinies; through views that lead to violence and bad rebirths (the "heavy fault"); behind the **wall** of sensual craving (the "middle fault"); and into the **moat** of ignorance in the higher realms (the "light fault"). The arhat is free of all four.

In brief: fools are ashamed of what is not shameful and not ashamed of what is, fear what is not to be feared and do not fear what is. Venerable Miào Jìng: Māra is the master of ordinary beings; the sage no longer belongs to him.

quiz.q: What are the four lines of the sixteenth verse?
options: space bears no bird's track; non-Buddhist paths have no true renunciant; fools delight in speculation; the Tathāgata has none
the sky has clouds, the earth mountains
quiz.why: "As space bears no trace of a bird's flight, so is there no true renunciant among non-Buddhist paths. Fools delight in idle speculation — but in the Tathāgata there is none." Master Cháng Bǎi: "renunciant" here means the noble path.

quiz.q: "虛空無鳥跡" is rendered "no trace of a bird's flight." How do the masters read it?
options: a bird in space has no place to rest — like beings seeking in saṃsāra with nowhere to settle
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: in space there is no place for a bird to dwell — describing how people seek on and on in saṃsāra and in the end have nowhere to rest. Venerable Miào Jìng: a bird flying in space has no place to settle. The prose has "no foothold"; the English "trace" drifts from it.

quiz.q: What does Master Cháng Bǎi say "renunciant" means in "no renunciant among outsiders"?
options: the noble path — outsiders lack it
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: outsiders have no śramaṇa — śramaṇa here is the noble path.

quiz.q: The English limits "no renunciant" to non-Buddhist paths. Does Venerable Miào Jìng limit it so?
options: no — those who wear robes and call themselves Buddhists yet pursue wrong views also have no śramaṇa
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: he wears monastic robes and says he is the Buddha's disciple, but what he studies is wrong view. The treatise says those who pursue a wrong holy life even within the well-taught Dharma also have no śramaṇa; the English is too narrow.

quiz.q: How does the seventeenth verse describe the true sage?
options: free of every abode and speculation, crossing wall and moat, free of craving — the sage wanders the world unrecognized by gods or men
living in mountains, served by gods
quiz.why: "Free of every abode, free of all idle speculation, having crossed the wall and the moat, free of craving — the sage wanders the world, unrecognized by gods or men." Master Cháng Bǎi: "true" means not false; muni means silent one.

quiz.q: What do the wall and the moat stand for, and how do the masters differ?
options: Cháng Bǎi: the wall is sensual craving, the moat craving for form and formless existence; Miào Jìng: the moat stands for ignorance
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the wall stands for sensual craving — the wall surrounding and protecting the city; the moat stands for craving for form and formless existence. Venerable Miào Jìng: what does the moat stand for? Ignorance. The two readings differ.

quiz.q: The sage is free of "Māra's enmity." What, per Venerable Miào Jìng, is the relationship between ordinary beings and Māra?
options: Māra is the master of ordinary beings; they belong to him and he decides for them
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: Māra is the master of ordinary beings; they take Māra as their lord and belong to him, and he decides for them. The sage is free of this subjection — which is why gods cannot recognise him.
